public_rationale: The records establish an August 7 release, earlier changes of plan, and a troubled reception. They also contain positive benchmark results. This supports a narrower description of a disappointing rollout. It does not settle whether GPT-5 was late against a particular public deadline or fell short of an identifiable capability expectation. Selecting those standards for Marcus would determine the result.
limitations: The primary Reddit discussion was inaccessible; launch-reception evidence relies on contemporary reporting.
A poor rollout and a failure to deliver expected model capabilities are related but distinct claims.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-5, released in August 2025, arrived late and did not meet expectations.

statement.excerpt: August, 2025: GPT-5 came late and fell short.
statement.document_title: Game over. AGI is not imminent, and LLMs are not the royal road to getting there.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that GPT-5 arrived later than publicly communicated expectations and delivered less capability than its public buildup led people to expect.
Public statements by OpenAI provide the comparison for timing and capability expectations; the claim does not identify a particular promise.
The surrounding discussion of AGI makes capability relevant, but does not establish that OpenAI promised GPT-5 would achieve AGI.
The target period is its August 2025 launch and initial performance.
criteria.support_condition: An identifiable earlier launch expectation was missed, and launch evidence shows a material shortfall against identifiable public capability expectations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The release met the relevant public timing expectation and demonstrated the capabilities used as the expectation baseline. Evidence can contradict either component separately.
